paths.better-auth: Only packages/core/src/auth/better-auth.ts may import this. Everything else goes through the packages/core/auth seam, so swapping provider stays a bounded job. See research/07-auth-and-tenancy.md section 1.
paths.@better-auth/passkey: Same seam as better-auth, and the one people actually reach for: its client half exports startAuthentication({ useBrowserAutofill }), which is exactly what apps/web/src/components/auth/passkey.ts hand-rolls base64url to avoid. Only packages/core/src/auth/better-auth.ts may import it.
paths.@simplewebauthn/browser: A phantom dependency -- hoisted by @better-auth/passkey, declared in no package.json, and resolvable from apps/web. Its parseRequestOptionsFromJSON()/toJSON() were rejected on reach (Safari 17.4, Firefox 135), which is why passkey.ts encodes by hand. Importing it lands provider types in the app and undoes that decision silently.
paths.@simplewebauthn/server: Server half of the same phantom dependency. Verification belongs behind the seam in packages/core/src/auth/better-auth.ts, which is the only file allowed to know a WebAuthn library exists.
paths.@guestnote/db/unsafe: Bypasses tenant isolation. packages/db/** and the migration runner only. See research/05-architecture.md section 4.
paths.@aws-sdk/client-sesv2: Only packages/email/src/ses.ts may import this (and its test, to construct the SDK error classes it maps). Everything else goes through the packages/email seam, so swapping mail provider stays a bounded job -- and so the AWS SDK cannot be pulled into a bundle by a stray import. See research/05-architecture.md section 6.
paths.@sentry/nextjs: Only apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts may import this. lib/observability.ts was rewritten to take a reporter callback instead, because the SDK drags a webpack bundler plugin into its module graph and every test that transitively reached it failed with "The URL must be of scheme file" -- and because copy.ts refuses to ship a message catalogue to the login surface, so it will not have tens of kilobytes of SDK either. Same one-file-per-provider rule as better-auth and the AWS SDK; it was asserted in a comment and held by nothing until 2026-09-01.
